name: DIY Strawberry Liqueur

instructions.primary_message: Place the strawberries and tarragon in a sealable glass jar, then add vodka. Seal and shake. Let mixture steep for 2 days at room temperature away from direct sunlight. Strain strawberries and tarragon, then filter mixture through a coffee filter or through two layers of cheesecloth, pressing down to extract liquid.
Heat water and sugar in a pot on medium heat until it boils and forms a syrup, about 5 minutes. Let syrup cool.
Once the syrup is cool, combine it with the strawberry-tarragon infusion. Seal in bottle or jar, then shake to mix. Let rest for a minimum of 1 day. Store in the refrigerator for up to 2 months.

schema_metadata.keywords: cocktail ingredients, DIY vs Buy, liqueur, tarragon

description: To make a strawberry liqueur at home all you need is a few days and some ripe strawberries to a beverage less expensive and more delicious than anything you can find on a store shelf. This recipe pairs strawberries with fresh tarragon but you can use vanilla, basil, or mint.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 3 days 15 min.

Notes: If you're using frozen strawberries, defrost them before use.
If you can't find (or don't like) tarragon, other fresh herbs like basil or mint are good substitutes.
Be sure to strain thoroughly, as little floating bits of strawberry will give your liqueur an off-flavor after just a week or two.
author: Marcia Simmons
